import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1074

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1074](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1074)
-/

namespace Erdos1074

open scoped Nat
open Nat

/-- The EHS numbers (after Erdős, Hardy, and Subbarao) are those $m\geq 1$ such that there
exists a prime $p\not\equiv 1\pmod{m}$ such that $m! + 1 \equiv 0\pmod{p}$. -/
abbrev EHSNumbers : Set ℕ := {m | 1 ≤ m ∧ ∃ p, p.Prime ∧ ¬p ≡ 1 [MOD m] ∧ p ∣ m ! + 1}

/-- The Pillai primes are those primes $p$ such that there exists an $m \ge 1$ with
$p\not\equiv 1\pmod{m}$ such that $m! + 1 \equiv 0\pmod{p}$-/
abbrev PillaiPrimes : Set ℕ := {p | p.Prime ∧ ∃ m ≥ 1, ¬p ≡ 1 [MOD m] ∧ p ∣ m ! + 1}

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem two_not_mem_pillaiPrimes : ¬ 2 ∈ PillaiPrimes := by
  norm_num
  intro m hm h
  exact (Nat.dvd_factorial (by decide) (hm.lt_of_ne (by bound))).modEq_zero_nat.add_right 1

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem twentyThree_mem_pillaiPrimes : 23 ∈ PillaiPrimes := by
  norm_num
  use 14
  decide

/-- Let $S$ be the set of all $m\geq 1$ such that there exists a prime $p\not\equiv 1\pmod{m}$ such
that $m! + 1 \equiv 0\pmod{p}$. Does
$$
  \lim\frac{|S\cap[1, x]|}{x}
$$
exist? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1074.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c, EHSNumbers.HasDensity c := by
  sorry

/-- Let $S$ be the set of all $m\geq 1$ such that there exists a prime $p\not\equiv 1\pmod{m}$ such
that $m! + 1 \equiv 0\pmod{p}$. What is
$$
  \lim\frac{|S\cap[1, x]|}{x}?
$$ -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1074.parts.ii : EHSNumbers.HasDensity answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

/-- Similarly, if $P$ is the set of all primes $p$ such that there exists an $m$ with
$p\not\equiv 1\pmod{m}$ such that $m! + 1 \equiv 0\pmod{p}$, then does
$$
  \lim\frac{|P\cap[1, x]|}{\pi(x)}
$$
exist? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1074.parts.iii : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c, PillaiPrimes.HasDensity c {p | p.Prime} := by
  sorry

/-- Similarly, if $P$ is the set of all primes $p$ such that there exists an $m$ with
$p\not\equiv 1\pmod{m}$ such that $m! + 1 \equiv 0\pmod{p}$, then what is
$$
  \lim\frac{|P\cap[1, x]|}{\pi(x)}?
$$ -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1074.parts.iv :
    PillaiPrimes.HasDensity answer(sorry) {p | p.Prime} := by
  sorry

/-- Pillai [Pi30] raised the question of whether there exist any primes in $P$. This was answered
by Chowla, who noted that, for example, $14! + 1 \equiv 18! + 1 \equiv 0 \pmod{23}$. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1074.variants.mem_pillaiPrimes : 23 ∈ PillaiPrimes := by
  norm_num
  exact ⟨14, by decide⟩

/--
Erdős, Hardy, and Subbarao proved that $S$ is infinite.

Formal proof linked here provided by AlphaProof.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mzhorvath1/formal-conjectures/blob/3dec597bd1a73778760b761712a1fc5fb24bc5d7/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/1074.lean#L99"]
theorem erdos_1074.variants.EHSNumbers_infinite : EHSNumbers.Infinite := by
  sorry

/-- Erdős, Hardy, and Subbarao proved that $P$ is infinite. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1074.variants.PillaiPrimes_infinite : PillaiPrimes.Infinite := by
  sorry

/-- The sequence $S$ begins $8, 9, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, ...$ -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1074.variants.EHSNumbers_init :
    nth EHSNumbers '' (Set.Icc 0 6) = {8, 9, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17} := by
  sorry

/-- The sequence $P$ begins $23, 29, 59, 61, 67, 71, ...$ -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1074.variants.PillaiPrimes_init :
    nth PillaiPrimes '' (Set.Icc 0 5) = {23, 29, 59, 61, 67, 71} := by
  sorry

/-- Regarding the first question, Hardy and Subbarao computed all EHS numbers up to $2^{10}$, and
write "...if this trend conditions we expect [the limit] to be around 0.5, if it exists." -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1074.variants.EHSNumbers_one_half : EHSNumbers.HasDensity (1 / 2) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1074

findings.description: The declaration asserts that the EHS numbers have density exactly 1/2. It turns a tentative finite-data observation ('around 0.5, if it exists') into an exact conjecture and omits the source's explicit subsequent conjecture that the density is 1. These are incompatible limiting-density claims, not equivalent formulations. A scratch Lean proof confirms that EHSNumbers.HasDensity (1 / 2) and EHSNumbers.HasDensity 1 cannot both hold.
findings.source_evidence: Hardy–Subbarao, 'A Modified Problem of Pillai and Some Related Questions', American Mathematical Monthly 109 (2002), §3(B), p. 557: after the tentative 'around 0.5' observation, they say that the occurrence of EHS numbers 'makes us believe that their asymptotic density exists and is unity. Erdős, though initially hesitant, later agreed with this view.' Appendix 4(i), p. 558, quotes Erdős's July 29, 1993 letter conjecturing the defining property for almost all n. Author-hosted paper: https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~subbarao/documents/2002_Pillai.pdf . The full passage is also reproduced at https://www.erdosproblems.com/1074 .
findings.suggested_fix: Replace this variant with the density-one conjecture, `EHSNumbers.HasDensity 1`, and update its name and docstring accordingly. The tentative 'around 0.5' observation can remain historical commentary, but should not be formalized as an exact density of 1/2.

reformulations.difference: Set.HasDensity uses strict natural-number cutoffs, counting S ∩ [0,n), rather than the source's inclusive interval [1,x].
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Since 0 ∉ EHSNumbers, its partial density at n+1 is |S ∩ [1,n]|/(n+1). Multiplication by (n+1)/n, which tends to 1, recovers the source's quotient. Integer and real cutoffs also give equivalent limits by taking the natural floor. The fixed-value equivalences and the resulting existence equivalence were checked in /workspace/review/density.lean.

reformulations.difference: The requested limiting value is expressed using HasDensity rather than an explicit limit of inclusive counting quotients.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The endpoint and real-cutoff equivalences hold uniformly for every c : ℝ: EHSNumbers.HasDensity c is equivalent to convergence of |S ∩ [1,x]|/x to c. Thus the real-valued answer slot specifies precisely the requested limit. Both integer- and real-cutoff equivalences were proved in /workspace/review/density.lean.

reformulations.difference: The source's denominator π(x) is represented by HasDensity relative to the set of primes, with strict cutoffs.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: PillaiPrimes is a subset of the primes, so the extra intersection with the reference set does not change the numerator. Its relative partial density at n+1 equals |P ∩ [1,n]|/π(n) exactly. Shifting the index preserves convergence; real cutoffs are handled by the natural floor. These equivalences, including existence of the limit, were checked in /workspace/review/density.lean.

reformulations.difference: The numerical answer is specified as a relative HasDensity value instead of an explicit limit divided by π(x).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Uniformly for c : ℝ, the exact identity between relative partial density at n+1 and |P ∩ [1,n]|/π(n), followed by index shifting and passage to real cutoffs, identifies this predicate with the source's limit having value c. The equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/density.lean.

sources_consulted: G. E. Hardy and M. V. Subbarao, A Modified Problem of Pillai and Some Related Questions, American Mathematical Monthly 109(6) (2002), 554–559: https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~subbarao/documents/2002_Pillai.pdf

https://oeis.org/A063980 — full entry read through https://r.jina.ai/http://oeis.org/A063980
https://erdosproblems.com/bibs/HaSu02 — bibliography entry read through Jina Reader
https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/pdf/10.1080/00029890.2002.11919885 — publisher access page read through Jina Reader; the full article was subsequently obtained from the author-hosted URL
review.notes: Checked all 14 declarations. Apart from the listed density variant, the definitions, questions, infinitude results, and tests agree with the sources. Computable predicates proved equivalent to the two definitions reproduce [8,9,13,14,15,16,17] and [23,29,59,61,67,71]. Lean checks also cover boundary exclusions, the necessary witness bound m < p, uniqueness of density values, and their bounds in [0,1]. The density-equivalence proofs have no sorry dependencies. Scratch files are /workspace/review/scratch.lean and /workspace/review/density.lean; the target file remains identical to its committed blob. The current Erdős page records the density questions as open, and Hardy–Subbarao Theorems 2.1 and 2.12 support the solved infinitude tags. The linked external formal-proof artifact was not audited.

submission.summary: Changed the variant to `EHSNumbers.HasDensity 1`, renamed it to `Erdos1074.erdos_1074.variants.EHSNumbers_one`, and updated its docstring to state the Hardy–Subbarao–Erdős density-one conjecture. Preserved the research-open and AMS attributes and left all other declarations unchanged. The required compile command succeeds with only `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.
